description: We work with visual demonstrations, games and real world projects.
summary:
ORBITAL is an interactive space mission design game that puts players in control of their own Earth-observation satellite mission.

Players take on the role of a mission designer, building a spacecraft by selecting scientific instruments, power systems, batteries, communications equipment, and an orbit. Every decision affects the spacecraft's resources and its ability to complete the mission.

After passing resource checks, players launch their satellite and enter an interactive simulation where they track its journey, collect observations based on historical NASA wildfire data, manage onboard resources, and transmit information to ground stations. A mission debrief then evaluates the results, explains what worked and what failed, and encourages players to improve their design.

By turning complex satellite engineering decisions into an interactive, learn-by-doing experience, ORBITAL makes space technology and Earth observation more accessible, engaging, and understandable.
details:
ORBITAL: Mission 001 — Earth Watch is an interactive satellite mission design game built to make space engineering accessible through hands-on experimentation.

How it works

The player begins with a mission briefing: monitor wildfire activity across Western North America. They then enter the spacecraft design studio, where they configure four key areas: scientific payload, orbit, power systems, and communications. Each choice affects the spacecraft's mass, cost, power requirements, and data capacity.

Once the design passes resource validation, the player launches the spacecraft and enters an interactive 2D orbital simulation. They can follow the satellite's movement, observe its coverage, track detected thermal anomalies from historical NASA FIRMS data, monitor onboard resources, and transmit collected information through ground stations.

After the simulation, the mission debrief presents performance metrics, explains successes and failures, and helps players understand how their engineering decisions affected the outcome. Players can then redesign their spacecraft and attempt the mission again.

What makes ORBITAL different

ORBITAL turns satellite engineering from something people only read about into something they can actively experience. Instead of simply showing information about spacecraft, it lets players make engineering decisions and see their consequences. The combination of spacecraft building, resource management, orbital visualization, mission operations, and performance analysis creates an engaging learning experience.

Intended impact

The project aims to spark curiosity about space technology, satellite engineering, and Earth's changing environment. It helps students and space enthusiasts understand how satellites support Earth observation and why successful missions require careful planning and trade-offs.

Technology used

The project was developed using React, Vite, JavaScript, Zustand, p5.js, and Tailwind CSS. It uses locally stored JSON data and browser-based storage to support the interactive experience.

Scientific foundation

The mission uses a historical 2025 snapshot of NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m active-fire observations from Western North America. The orbital and spacecraft systems are simplified educational simulations designed to demonstrate engineering concepts rather than reproduce the full complexity of an operational space mission.
